teams.heading: Manager Lionel Danford seeks $70,000 for Fiji deaf rugby sevens tour
teams.body: The Fiji men’s and women’s deaf rugby sevens teams require up to $70,000 to fund their upcoming World Deaf Rugby Sevens Championship campaign in Tokyo. Team manager Lionel Danford confirmed that a significant funding gap remains for daily expenses and training camps, stating, "We are still looking for funds." As part of their build-up for the tournament starting later this month, both squads recently scrimmaged against Osea Kolinisau’s national sevens side to sharpen technical skills and provide deaf players an opportunity to impress national selectors.

lead.why: It details a significant financial shortfall for a national representative side and their recent high-profile preparation with the senior sevens squad.

teams.heading: Ollie Sleightholme and Alex Coles impress Steve Borthwick in Premiership thriller
teams.body: England internationals Ollie Sleightholme and Alex Coles have issued a timely reminder of their quality ahead of the November tests following Northampton Saints' 71-48 victory over Bath. Sleightholme scored a hat-trick and beat 11 defenders, showcasing the form that first brought him into the Test picture in 2024. Meanwhile, Coles continues to be an integral figure for the Saints, earning praise for his work rate at the lineout and his ability to influence the game in both tight and open play.

teams.heading: Victor Wembanyama joins Provence Rugby sessions to develop physical movement patterns
teams.body: NBA star Victor Wembanyama utilised his recent summer break to sharpen his conditioning through an immersive stint with second-tier side Provence. The 7ft 4in forward participated in line-out drills, tackle-pad sessions, and passing exercises, reportedly seeking to improve his stability and movement patterns. Wembanyama, who previously toured China to study strength training, praised the squad’s internal camaraderie after his time with the club. Provence have made a strong start to their domestic season, remaining unbeaten through their opening five league fixtures.

teams.heading: Bundee Aki and Connacht struggle as Glasgow Warriors dominate forward battle
teams.body: Connacht suffered a 36-19 defeat to Glasgow in Friday's URC fixture, as the visitors were "mauled to death" at Scotstoun. The hosts secured four of their five tries from lineout mauls, leaving Connacht struggling to contain the set-piece power. Despite two tries from Josh Ioane, the visitors could not overcome the early deficit created by Glasgow’s forward control. The match also saw Bundee Aki involved in a late-game outburst as his side fell to a disappointing result on the road.

teams.heading: Italy maintains high-water mark for best-ever international world ranking position
teams.body: Italy currently holds a benchmark for their historical performance in the men's international game, having reached a best-ever world ranking of No. 8. The team achieved this significant position twice, first in 2007 and more recently in 2024. As the squad prepares for upcoming fixtures, this historical high point remains a reference for the nation's progress within the international rugby hierarchy.

teams.heading: Josh McKay emerges as potential option for Scotland’s full-back spot
teams.body: Glasgow’s Josh McKay is increasingly tipped for a call-up to the Scotland squad for the upcoming November internationals. While Blair Kinghorn remains the established first-choice full-back, McKay’s consistent domestic form has highlighted his value in a competitive position alongside Kyle Rowe and Tom Jordan. With the 2027 World Cup now on the horizon, coaches are prioritising opportunities to test depth in the international arena, making the upcoming autumn window a critical period for evaluating new additions to the backline.

teams.heading: Aaron Wainwright shines as Wales stars influence Leicester’s Gallagher Premiership victory
teams.body: Aaron Wainwright impressed for Leicester Tigers on Friday, scoring his first try for the club and completing 14 tackles during their 38-31 win against Gloucester. He was joined by fellow Welshmen Tommy Reffell, who delivered an all-action performance at the breakdown, and Olly Cracknell, who contributed 16 tackles and 14 carries. The performance keeps Reffell firmly in the frame for a Wales starting jersey, as he continues to press his case ahead of the upcoming Nations Championship block.

teams.heading: Shaun Edwards and Mario Ledesma join Felipe Contepomi’s Argentina backroom staff
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has strengthened his backroom team ahead of the upcoming Nations Championship fixtures by appointing Shaun Edwards as defence coach and Mario Ledesma as forwards coach. Edwards joins on a deal running until the end of the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia following his departure from France earlier this year. Ledesma, who previously served as Argentina head coach from 2018 to 2022, returns to national service to oversee the pack until the tournament concludes.

teams.heading: Les Kiss backs Wallabies to return fire after Eden Park defeat
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has turned his focus to next weekend's Bledisloe Cup rematch in Sydney following a heavy 50-19 defeat to the All Blacks at Eden Park. Australia led 14-17 at half-time after tries from Tom Wright and Harry Wilson, but a dominant second-half display from the hosts extended New Zealand's unbeaten run at the venue to 54 Tests. Kiss remained defiant after suffering his first loss at the helm, telling reporters: "We’ll go back and we’ll work on what we have to and try and turn the dial in the right areas that can go to Sydney and return fire."

teams.heading: Japan Rugby League One Relents on Foreign-Born Player Rules After Backlash
teams.body: Japan Rugby League One has backtracked on contentious player registration rules that would have classified naturalized players as foreigners despite holding Japanese passports, following a fierce backlash from fans and players. Managing Executive Director Hajime Shoji acknowledged shortcomings in the rollout, stating, "We lacked communication with players who would be adversely affected by the changes. We would like to reflect on that." The top-tier tournament announced that naturalized players who acquired citizenship by May 2025 will now be treated the same as Japanese-born players.

teams.heading: New Zealand close gap on the Springboks in World Rugby rankings
teams.body: Following their dominant 50-19 victory over Australia at Eden Park, New Zealand have added 0.66 to their rating to reach 91.81. Dave Rennie's side sit just over a point behind South Africa, who occupy the summit on 93.09. With the world champions facing demanding November fixtures away to Ireland and France in the Nations Championship, the All Blacks have positioned themselves firmly in the race to finish the year at No. 1.

teams.heading: Johan Ackermann praises returning Springboks as Bulls crush Lions
teams.body: Returning Springboks hit the ground running in the United Rugby Championship as the Bulls secured a 57-15 victory over the Lions at Loftus Versfeld. Gerhard Steenekamp and Johan Grobbelaar starred in the tight exchanges, while Cameron Hanekom and Canan Moodie made an impact on attack. Replacements Marco van Staden, Cobus Wiese, Elrigh Louw and Handré Pollard added further momentum off the bench as the hosts ran in tries through Harold Vorster, Grobbelaar, Hanekom, Jeandre Rudolph, Moodie, JF van Heerden, Cheswill Jooste and Sebastian de Klerk.
